scenes.heading: Filters
scenes.narration: Dispatcher. Filters. In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What does the /filter section specify in Dispatcher?
scenes.heading: The /filter section specifies which HTTP requests Dispatcher accepts
scenes.body: Section 5 says the /filter section specifies which HTTP requests Dispatcher accepts.

scenes.question: What happens to requests that are not accepted by the /filter section?
scenes.heading: Requests that are not accepted are sent back to the web server with a 404 status

scenes.question: If there is no /filter section at all, how does Dispatcher behave?
scenes.heading: If there is no /filter section, all requests are accepted
scenes.body: Section 5 says that if there is no /filter section, all requests are accepted.

scenes.question: What allowlist strategy does the speech recommend for /filter rules?
scenes.heading: Use an allowlist strategy: first deny everything, then allow only what is needed

scenes.question: What is the classic first deny-all rule described in the speech?
scenes.heading: The first deny-all rule is type deny with url asterisk

scenes.question: Which request-line elements are preferred for filtering instead of matching the whole line?
scenes.heading: The preferred request-line elements are /method, /url, /query, /protocol, /path, /selectors, /extension, and /suffix
scenes.body: Section 5 says filtering on elements of the request line is preferred, naming /method, /url, /query, /protocol, and from Dispatcher 4.2.0 also /path, /selectors, /extension, and /suffix.

scenes.heading: Quick recap
items: The /filter section specifies which HTTP requests Dispatcher accepts
Requests that are not accepted are sent back to the web server with a 404 status
If there is no /filter section, all requests are accepted
Use an allowlist strategy: first deny everything, then allow only what is needed
The first deny-all rule is type deny with url asterisk
The preferred request-line elements are /method, /url, /query, /protocol, /path, /selectors, /extension, and /suffix
The older /glob should be avoided because it matches the entire request line, is deprecated, and can lead to security issues
